changes.before: are likely to warrant exceptionally low levels for the federal funds rate at least through mid-2013.
changes.after: are likely to warrant exceptionally low levels for the federal funds rate at least through late 2014.
the Committee expects to maintain a highly accommodative stance for monetary policy.

changes.before: The Committee continues to expect a moderate pace of economic growth over coming quarters
changes.after: The Committee expects economic growth over coming quarters to be modest

changes.before: Inflation has moderated since earlier in the year, and longer-term inflation expectations have remained stable.
changes.after: Inflation has been subdued in recent months, and longer-term inflation expectations have remained stable.

changes.before: However, the Committee will continue to pay close attention to the evolution of inflation and inflation expectations.
The Committee also anticipates that inflation will settle, over coming quarters, at levels at or below those consistent with the Committee’s dual mandate.
changes.after: The Committee also anticipates that over coming quarters, inflation will run at levels at or below those consistent with the Committee's dual mandate.

changes.before: but business fixed investment appears to be increasing less rapidly
changes.after: but growth in business fixed investment has slowed

changes.before: Voting against the action was Charles L. Evans, who supported additional policy accommodation at this time.
changes.after: Voting against the action was Jeffrey M. Lacker, who preferred to omit the description of the time period over which economic conditions are likely to warrant exceptionally low levels of the federal funds rate.

parsed.rationale: The forward guidance for near-zero rates was extended by about 18 months, from mid-2013 to late 2014, alongside a new commitment to a highly accommodative stance, a downgrade of the growth outlook, and removal of the inflation-vigilance sentence. Together these mark a clear dovish change in guidance, only slightly offset by a hawkish dissent.
